subject: ss-neurosurgery
title: Low-grade glioma and oligodendroglioma: molecules, PCV, resection and transformation

steps.say: IDH mutation with codeletion is defining oligodendroglioma while ATRX loss is defining astrocytoma. Wildtype low-grade histology is behaving aggressively and it is managed as high grade. Testing is ordered on every diffuse glioma.
steps.tx: **IDH mutation** with 1p19q codeletion defines oligodendroglioma, IDH mutation with ATRX and TP53 loss defines astrocytoma, and IDH-wildtype low-grade histology behaves aggressively and is managed as high grade. Molecular testing therefore precedes every treatment plan. Histology alone no longer decides therapy.

rows: IDH mutant plus ATRX and TP53 lost

steps.say: Oligodendrogliomas are calcifying in most cases and they are favouring the frontal lobe. Fried-egg cells with chicken-wire vessels are seen under the microscope. A calcified frontal mass is the classic exam image.
steps.tx: Oligodendrogliomas calcify in most cases with a fried egg histology of honeycomb cells and chicken-wire vessels, and frontal location with **calcification** on CT is the classic exam image. Calcification is visible on plain CT before contrast. The combination points to oligo over astrocytoma.

steps.say: Two landmark trials are proving that PCV chemotherapy with radiotherapy is markedly improving survival in codeleted tumours, doubling it in one trial. PCV is remaining a standard option for high-risk oligodendroglioma. Radiotherapy alone is now considered undertreatment.
steps.tx: RTOG 9402 and EORTC 26951 proved radiotherapy plus **PCV chemotherapy** markedly improves survival in codeleted oligodendroglioma (doubling it in RTOG 9402), making PCV a standard option for high-risk oligodendroglioma. Both trials matured over decades of follow-up. Long survivors justify the upfront toxicity.

steps.say: High risk is defined by age above forty or any subtotal resection. Such patients are receiving adjuvant therapy rather than observation. Young fully resected cases are watched closely instead.
steps.tx: The RTOG **high-risk low-grade** definition is age above 40 or any subtotal resection, and such low-grade gliomas get adjuvant radiotherapy plus chemotherapy rather than observation. Either factor alone triggers treatment. Neither youth nor gross imaging clearance alone earns observation when resection was partial.

steps.say: Gross total resection is improving survival and seizure control together. Mapping is used whenever the tumour is bordering language or movement. Eloquent remnants are watched or irradiated by molecular risk.
steps.tx: **Gross total resection** improves survival and seizure control and is pursued with mapping when feasible, while eloquent residual disease is watched or irradiated based on molecular risk. Awake mapping protects language during dominant-side surgery. Seizure freedom often follows complete removal.

vis.alt: Axial MRI of a cystic ganglioglioma with an enhancing mural nodule beside histology showing dysplastic neurons and a glial component.
vis.caption: Cystic ganglioglioma with mural nodule (a glioneuronal tumour, not a diffuse glioma); well-circumscribed lesions like this suit gross total resection. Credit: StewardMD. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Vorasidenib is a brain-penetrant IDH inhibitor that is delaying progression after surgery. The INDIGO trial is supporting its use in grade 2 IDH-mutant disease. Young observed patients are gaining a targeted option.
steps.tx: **Vorasidenib**, a brain-penetrant IDH inhibitor, delays progression in grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma after surgery per INDIGO, opening targeted therapy for young observed patients. It postpones radiotherapy and its cognitive cost. Scans continue on schedule during treatment. Monitoring continues because resistance eventually emerges.

steps.say: Fits are presenting most low-grade gliomas before any scan is ordered. Levetiracetam is first choice because it is avoiding enzyme induction. Inducing agents are clashing with chemotherapy metabolism.
steps.tx: Seizures are the presenting symptom in most low-grade gliomas and **levetiracetam** is first-line, with enzyme-inducing antiepileptics avoided during chemotherapy because of interactions. Control also guides surgical urgency. Monotherapy is preferred and levels are rarely needed. Breakthrough fits prompt dose review and imaging.

vis.alt: Brain illustration showing an epileptogenic focus with glutamate excitation, reduced GABA inhibition, thalamocortical spread and spike-wave discharge.
vis.caption: Epileptogenic focus with hypersynchronous spread explains presenting seizures. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: New enhancement with rising choline and clinical decline is signalling malignant transformation. Re-resection is planned with fresh molecular testing. CDKN2A loss is confirming higher grade.
steps.tx: **Malignant transformation** declares itself with new enhancement, rising choline and clinical deterioration, prompting re-resection and molecular retesting for CDKN2A loss and higher grade. Transformation changes prognosis and therapy entirely. Never assume the original grade still applies. Multidisciplinary review resets the plan after retesting.
